adhere

/ad-HEER/ - rhymes with appear · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Adhere means to follow a rule or standard closely.

The pharmacy adheres to a two-person count for every controlled prescription, no matter how long the line grows.

Example

The station adheres to its seven-second delay for every live guest, even the mayor — the engineer who once switched it off spent a decade explaining why.

Adhere is stricter than follow: following a rule leaves room for judgment and the occasional exception, while adhering to it means every step, every time, exactly as written. The word even sounds like what it means — you stick to the rule.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

obey: Obey means doing what an authority tells you — a person gives the order and you carry it out, and the relationship is the point. Adhere points at the standard itself rather than a boss: you adhere to a code or protocol, exactly and without exceptions.

conform: Conform means matching the general expectations around you — dressing, speaking, and behaving roughly the way the group does. Adhere is narrower and stricter: you adhere to a specific written rule or standard, every step carried out exactly as it says.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

violate: to break the rule outright

breach: the formal word for the same break, common in law and contracts

Where it sits · how strictly conduct keeps to the rule

notice → follow → adhere

notice vs. adhere: Merely noticing a rule is much weaker than adhering to it — noticing means you only know the rule is posted, while adhere means your conduct keeps to it exactly, every time.

follow vs. adhere: Follow stops short of adhere — you keep to the rule in the main, with room for judgment at the edges.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ad-: to

Root — her-: to stick

Put it together: Ad- (to) + her- (to stick) = to stick to. Latin adhaerere described glue before it described character: things that adhere are stuck fast. English kept both pictures — tape adheres to a wall, and a pilot adheres to a checklist — the second is just the first moved into conduct.

Use the root in a new word: adhesive: The label's adhesive gave out in the heat, and the sticker curled off the jar.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / procedural

Adhere always travels with to — you adhere to a rule, a code, a deadline — and it claims exactness: every step, every time, no exceptions. For casual talk, follow or stick to is plainer; save adhere for protocols, contracts, and standards where the letter of the rule matters.
